Service Discovery — Before and After, Third Pass

The evening of 9 September 2026. This page is self-contained: every picture is inside the file, so it opens anywhere.

1 · The option pages — no "Against it", plain words

The review asked for the verdicts to come out. Each option page now says what it is, how it works and why it helps, in words a school-leaver can read. What each option needs before it can be built is on one page near the end, not repeated on every option.

2 · Two Questions — the answer screen

Both answers are shown under "You chose". Three schemes, each with View details. No apply button: the scheme's own page says where to apply. One link opens the Schemes page filtered to the same two answers. The scheme type is no longer on every card, because every scheme here is centrally backed.

3 · One Tap — the group's portal first

A band at the top carries the one portal or helpline the Department runs for that group, where it has one. A button appears only where the site answered when checked; otherwise the portal is named in words. Below it, the schemes sorted by what they give, each with View details.

4 · The Schemes page — the earlier layouts, with the feedback applied

Option A keeps its row of faces and cards; Option B keeps its filter panel and table. Both now filter on the two lists only, show no counts, grey out a filter that would leave nothing, page their results, and read every field from the scheme master. The faces sit on one grid with a fixed label height, so the row is aligned whatever the name.
